cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, gets a new message from the LORD. It's for Moses' brother Aaron, Aaron's sons and all the Israelites. That's the WHOLE group chat, friend, so nobody gets to say they missed the message.
Here's the first rule, and it's about where. Say someone from the house of Israel slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat, in the camp or outside of it.

cards.question: God says the ox, lamb or goat has to be brought somewhere to be presented as an offering to the LORD. Where?

answers.text: The entrance to the Tent of Meeting
The banks of the Jordan River

cards.question: God says a man who slaughters the animal without bringing it there has shed blood and must be cut off from his people.
God says the Israelites will now bring the LORD the sacrifices they've been offering somewhere else. Where have they been offering them?

cards.text: Now they bring them to the priest at the entrance, as peace offerings. The priest splatters the blood on the LORD's altar and burns the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, and friend, I've chased a pleasing aroma my WHOLE life and the best I ever did was a kitchen that smelled like chocolate chips.

cards.question: Then God names what has to stop. Who must the Israelites no longer offer their sacrifices to?
God says this rule about where to bring sacrifices only lasts as long as Moses leads Israel.

cards.text: Then God adds burnt offerings and every other sacrifice. Same deal: if it doesn't come to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, that man is cut off from his people.

cards.question: The rule about bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices to the Tent of Meeting also covers foreigners living among the Israelites.

cards.text: Now God turns to blood. If anyone eats any blood, Israelite or foreigner, God says, "I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people." Friend, when the God who made everything says that, you do NOT want to be that person.

cards.question: Then God explains why eating blood is off-limits. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The life of the flesh is in the blood
Blood is set aside for the priests alone
Blood spreads sickness through the camp

cards.question: God says He has given the Israelites the blood for a purpose on the altar. What is it?

answers.text: To make atonement for their souls
To mark the borders of their camp
To seal their treaties with other nations

cards.text: So God says it again: no Israelite and no foreigner living among them may eat blood. Then He gets to hunting, when someone brings down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten.

cards.question: What must the hunter do with the blood of the wild animal or bird he brings down?

answers.text: Drain it and cover it with dirt

cards.question: God's rule against eating blood only covers oxen, lambs and goats.

cards.text: Then a different case. Someone, native or foreigner, eats an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts, so he has to wash his clothes and bathe with water.

cards.question: After he washes his clothes and bathes, how long is the person who ate the dead animal unclean?
And if that person skips washing his clothes and bathing, what happens?

answers.text: He owes the priest a goat
He must sleep outside the camp

cards.text: That's the end of this message, friend. But trust me, the LORD's not done talking to Moses, so keep that apron on.
